items.headline: Gasoline-like smell blankets parts of central Singapore overnight; NEA says air quality normal
items.summary: The NEA said it received feedback about a gas or chemical smell across parts of the central region late on July 16, but reported air quality stayed within the usual range as it worked to trace the source.

items.headline: Man, 22, jailed more than nine years with caning for raping two 13-year-old girls
items.summary: A 22-year-old man was sentenced to more than nine years' jail and 12 strokes of the cane after being convicted of raping two 13-year-old girls, in a case reported by The Straits Times.

items.headline: Teen and four men arrested over Singpass accounts funnelled to an overseas scam syndicate
items.summary: Police arrested a 17-year-old girl and four men aged 22 to 29 over the fraudulent handover of Singpass accounts to an overseas syndicate under the guise of job applications.

items.headline: Two Malaysian men brought to Singapore over government-impersonation scams tied to 50-plus cases
items.summary: Two Malaysian men, aged 38 and 44, were brought into Singapore for suspected involvement in government-official impersonation scams that police link to more than 50 reported cases.

items.headline: Drink-driver who fled nearly 10km after a crash jailed and banned for five years
items.summary: Xie Junliang, 43, was sentenced to jail and a five-year driving ban after rear-ending a motorcycle at a red light while drunk and fleeing the scene, injuring two people.

items.headline: SBI Funds Management's roughly $1 billion IPO, India's biggest of 2026, is subscribed 41.66 times
items.summary: The offering of India's largest asset manager, an SBI-Amundi JV, was subscribed 41.66 times and drew bids worth about 3 trillion rupees ($31 billion); shares list on July 21.

items.headline: Modi's cabinet clears a 1.9 trillion-rupee push to cut India's reliance on imports
items.summary: Modi's cabinet approved 1.9 trillion rupees ($19.7 billion) of extra support for domestic chip, smartphone and fertiliser production to shield supply chains after Strait of Hormuz disruption.

items.headline: India's inflation climbs above the RBI's 4% target for the first time in nearly 18 months
items.summary: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said supply-side pressures, higher oil and monsoon risks pushed inflation above the 4% target for the first time in about a year and a half, with the rupee past 96 to the dollar.

items.headline: Burnham confirmed as Labour leader, to become UK prime minister on Monday
items.summary: Andy Burnham was confirmed as leader of the governing Labour Party on July 17, vowing to beat Britain's new right, and is due to replace Keir Starmer in Downing Street on Monday, July 20.

items.headline: Burnham inherits a decade of political turmoil, with the economy, NHS and Reform UK all pressing
items.summary: As Burnham prepares to become Britain's seventh leader in a decade, analysts point to a struggling economy, strained NHS and the surging Reform UK party as the immediate tests of his premiership.

items.headline: Update: US launches a seventh straight night of strikes on Iran, hitting bridges near Bandar Abbas
items.summary: US Central Command struck dozens of targets including bridges around Bandar Abbas; Iranian state media reported at least eight killed and 20 wounded, and Kuwait said several of its troops were hurt in an Iranian attack.

items.headline: Update: Russian drones strike Mykolaiv port, killing two aboard a foreign ship, as Ukraine hits Black Sea vessels
items.summary: Russian drone attacks on Mykolaiv port killed two Ukrainians aboard a foreign-registered vessel, with further deaths in Kherson and Odesa, while Ukraine said its drones struck 12 Russian Black Sea vessels.

items.headline: Update: Israeli strikes kill at least 14 across Gaza, including a drone strike on a funeral procession
items.summary: At least 14 Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks on July 17, more than half when a drone struck a funeral procession in central Gaza; the Israeli military said it targeted a cell but was aware uninvolved people may have been harmed.

items.headline: FIFA opens an investigation into Argentina's 'Malvinas' banner at the World Cup semi-final
items.summary: FIFA is investigating Argentina after players unfurled a Las Malvinas son Argentinas banner following their July 15 semi-final win over England; Keir Starmer backed a probe while Javier Milei called it perfectly valid.

items.headline: Israel and Lebanon agree a framework to pull back from two southern 'pilot zones' at a sixth Rome round
items.summary: Lebanon and Israel concluded a sixth round of US-brokered Rome talks with agreement on withdrawing Israeli forces from two pilot zones; hours later Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel intends to remain in broader security zones.

items.headline: China's Moonshot unveils Kimi K3, the world's largest open-weight AI model, triggering a chip selloff
items.summary: Moonshot released Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter model it says rivals leading US systems; the launch drew DeepSeek-moment comparisons and pushed the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down about 5.7% into bear-market territory.

items.headline: Google's flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro is running months behind schedule
items.summary: Bloomberg reported Google is months late delivering Gemini 3.5 Pro, its most powerful model expected at May's developer conference; the delay, driven partly by coding work, has fed concern it is losing ground to Anthropic and OpenAI.

items.headline: Anthropic lines up investor meetings for a potential October IPO
items.summary: Bankers at Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan are scheduling investor meetings for a possible Anthropic listing as soon as October; the Claude maker was valued at $965 billion in a May round and has filed confidentially with the SEC.

items.headline: Identity startup Oak exits stealth with $60 million to secure AI agents
items.summary: Oak, co-founded by security entrepreneur Shai Morag, emerged from stealth with a $60 million seed round co-led by Accel, CRV and Greylock to build an AI-native identity platform governing human, machine and AI-agent access.

items.headline: Voice-AI startup Rime raises $24 million to field enterprise phone calls
items.summary: Rime, founded by Stanford speech scientists, raised a $24 million Series A led by M13; it says its speech models already power close to 100 million customer calls a month for clients including Mayo Clinic.

items.headline: TSMC posts a record Q2 profit, up 77%, and adds $100 billion to its Arizona plan
items.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor reported record Q2 net income of NT$706.6 billion, up 77%, with revenue up 36% on AI-chip demand; it lifted 2026 capex guidance to $60-$64 billion and pledged an extra $100 billion for Arizona.

items.headline: Brent crude jumps 4.6% to $88 after Kuwait reports an Iranian attack on a power and water plant
items.summary: Brent rose about 4.6% to settle near $88.10 and WTI gained 4.5% to $82.49 on July 17 after Kuwait said Iran struck a power and desalination plant, deepening Strait of Hormuz supply fears.

items.headline: Travelers jumps 8% as Q2 profit climbs 46% on lower catastrophe losses
items.summary: Insurer Travelers posted Q2 net income of $2.21 billion, up from $1.51 billion a year earlier, as catastrophe losses fell to $518 million from $927 million; the stock rose about 8%, leading the Dow.

items.headline: US retail sales cool to 0.2% in June as weekly jobless claims fall to 208,000
items.summary: US retail sales rose just 0.2% in June, the smallest gain in five months as gas-station receipts dropped, while initial jobless claims fell to 208,000, below expectations.

items.headline: World Cup final set: Spain to face Argentina at MetLife on Sunday after Argentina end England
items.summary: Argentina beat England 2-1 in the semi-final, Lionel Messi setting up both late goals, to reach the July 19 final against Spain at MetLife Stadium; Spain have conceded just once all tournament.

items.headline: Antonelli tops second practice at Spa as Gasly crashes heavily
items.summary: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in Friday's second practice for the Belgian Grand Prix with a 1:45.944, edging Norris and Verstappen; the session was red-flagged twice, including a heavy Gasly crash at Fagnes.

items.headline: What Friday practice at Spa revealed ahead of qualifying
items.summary: Autosport's review of Friday running at the 2026 Belgian GP flagged Mercedes' pace, a hydraulic issue on Piastri's McLaren in first practice, and Gasly's crash, with qualifying on Saturday and the race Sunday.

items.headline: Cerundolo stuns Ruud to reach the Gstaad semi-finals
items.summary: Sixth seed Juan Manuel Cerundolo beat second seed Casper Ruud 3-6, 7-5, 6-2 to reach the Gstaad semi-finals on a day of upsets that also saw top seed Alexander Bublik go out.

items.headline: Rublev battles back to reach the Bastad quarter-finals
items.summary: Top seed Andrey Rublev recovered from a second-set stumble to beat Mattia Pellegrino and move into the Nordea Open quarter-finals in Bastad.

items.headline: Webb finds a lava world's atmosphere is surprisingly rich in volcanic hydrogen
items.summary: Observing five eclipses of the super-Earth 55 Cancri e, 41 light-years away, NASA's Webb telescope found an atmosphere unexpectedly rich in hydrogen shaped by gases escaping the molten interior, with hints volcanic outgassing forms temporary clouds.

items.headline: An AI screen flags more than 250,000 cancer papers as likely 'paper-mill' fakes
items.summary: A BMJ study led by QUT's Adrian Barnett applied machine learning to 2.6 million cancer papers from 1999-2024 and flagged about 9.9%, more than 250,000, as bearing paper-mill hallmarks; Nature reported they draw roughly double the citations of genuine work.

items.headline: NASA astronaut Anil Menon and two cosmonauts reach the ISS, raising the crew to 10
items.summary: Anil Menon and Roscosmos cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina docked at the ISS aboard Soyuz MS-29 after a three-hour flight from Baikonur, temporarily lifting the lab's crew to 10 before a scheduled handover.

items.headline: Serbia becomes the 69th nation to sign the Artemis Accords
items.summary: Serbia signed the Artemis Accords at NASA headquarters in Washington on July 16, with Foreign Minister Marko Djuric signing on the country's behalf, joining the US-led framework for responsible space exploration.

fun_fact.headline: Nintendo was founded in 1889 as a playing-card company
fun_fact.body: Nintendo, the company behind Mario and the Switch, was founded in 1889, the same year the Eiffel Tower was completed, and spent its first several decades making hand-crafted hanafuda playing cards. Founder Fusajiro Yamauchi made the cards from mulberry-bark paper in Kyoto; the firm only pivoted to electronic toys and games in the 1960s and 1970s.

puzzle.title: Bankrupt at the Hotel
puzzle.body: A man is slowly pushing his car along a road. The moment he reaches a hotel, he announces that he is bankrupt. No crime has taken place, he is not upset, and everything he says is true. Why is he bankrupt, and why was he pushing the car?
puzzle.approach: Every literal detail is true, but the car, the hotel and the bankruptcy needn't be life-size.
puzzle.answer: He is playing Monopoly. His token, the little car, has landed on a property with a hotel on it that he cannot afford the rent for, bankrupting him. He was pushing the car only in the sense of moving his game piece around the board.

word_puzzle.title: Daily Bread
word_puzzle.body: Turn WHEAT into BREAD, one letter at a time. Each step changes exactly one letter and must be a valid English word. It can be done in seven steps.
word_puzzle.approach: Change exactly one letter at each step, keeping a real word every time.
word_puzzle.answer: WHEAT -> CHEAT -> CHEAP -> CHEEP -> CREEP -> CREED -> BREED -> BREAD (seven steps).

notes: India ran on fallback sources (CNBC, Bloomberg): all six primary Indian outlets (The Hindu, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, Times of India, NDTV, Economic Times) were unreachable from the routine environment. 3 verified domestic items cleared; fewer than the 4-item floor after exhausting reachable allowed/fallback outlets.

UK News ran on fallback sources (Al Jazeera, CNN): both primary outlets (BBC, Sky News) and The Guardian were unreachable. 2 verified UK-domestic items cleared; a strong TfL/Scattered Spider sentencing story was dropped for lack of an allowed or fallback-tier deep URL.
Singapore leaned on Mothership (an allowed source) as CNA/The Straits Times were hard to reach; the section skews to court and scam stories as a result.

Other Miscellaneous News leaned partly on NASA operational items (ISS crew arrival, Serbia Artemis Accords) alongside two frontier-science stories, because allowed frontier-science outlets were hard to source with in-window deep URLs.
Global carries four rolling-conflict updates (Iran, Ukraine, Gaza, Lebanon), each with a concrete new development, plus the FIFA/Malvinas story.
Multiple retry attempts were made per FIX 6 for the source-blocked sections; the routine's own live web search was used for second-source verification of every marquee item.
Belgian Grand Prix at Spa confirmed as the current F1 round via Formula1.com; qualifying (Sat) and race (Sun) had not yet run at publish time, so Sports carries Friday practice items.
